title: A River Called Anywhere
content:
A river called "anywhere" traverses an unknown prairie
Confined by its size and its will
Through valleys and hills it wanders
Longing for the mighty Ocean

I sit upon the fallen trunk of a fearsome Oak
I surrender to the current of the narrow brook
Adrift in search of a foreign sea
Longing for emancipation

A seagull flashes its brilliant wings overhead
Hope strikes the deepest corridors of my heart
The stream follows my strides onward
The graceful bird rides on a stream of salty perfume

I feel the stream widen and fall still
The delta reveals an infinite sea of diamonds and pearls
The undertow carries me wherever I command
I look up at the seagull and extend to it a smile of gratitude

I am free at last.

title: A Stranger in New Orleans
content:
How strange is this place,
where distant strangers meet momentarily,
their web-like lives of infinite complexity
intersecting at a point, as conjoined manifolds?

Strangers come and acquaintances go.
Though we met eyes only for a brief moment,
we share a common understanding;
though we walked in parallel for one mere evening,
we are friends nonetheless;
connected by our respective similarities,
enriched by our respective differences.

People come from the world around for reasons abound,
and yet we all ended up here,
in the same city,
in the same hostel,
in the same billiards hall,
at the very same time.

title: Alaska
content:
The streets are decked with starstruck folks,
Seeking escape from the air that chokes,
Wondering where they can tie their yokes,
They never have been to Alaska.

Some dream in the night, some say it feels right,
Some wander around, just barely upright,
Some get their desire from heavenly light,
They all want to go to Alaska.

Some go by sky, some go by water,
Some say it's cold, some say it gets hotter,
Some drive all the way, with son and with daughter,
They make their way to Alaska.

A poet does cry, at stories untold,
A gambler raises, while other ones fold,
A mother comforts the child that she holds,
They search for their homes in Alaska.

A river runs fast, a glacier runs slow,
the oceans run high, the Northern Lights glow,
A body is trembling, from bare head to toe,
They've all found their homes in Alaska.

title: An Unempty Forest
content:
A man walks alone on a moonlit forest trail
Searching for shelter, alas to no avail
Tomorrow he will find it, for he can never fail
But tonight, he knows, he must bear the wind and hail

The forest's gentle melodies creep throughout the air
Of a hidden watcher, the man is unaware
A sense of unknown company warns him to prepare
For it is still uncertain how deftly he will fare

The watcher breaks the shadows of an oak tree most sublime
In silence so supreme that one could sense a fallen dime
I cannot think of many ways to carry on the rhyme
For he, like me, does find himself so very short on time

title: Call of the Wild
content:
Marble and lumber comprise mighty halls
People do slumber behind stucco walls

Dark ears fall deaf to the tune of a bird
Perverse in the manner of words overheard

To run and to yell is to set free desire
To hasten to fall, to fall to the mire

Above the rustled and chirping birds fly
An unheard attempt to pierce through the sky

A blanket, a layer, to keep safe our home
At night, a shroud to protect those who roam

Aloof from the river, whose melody cries
For faraway places where tall mountains rise

And fall to the valleys, so green and so vast
Where trickling rivers descend oh-so fast

The sun paints the wheat hues of sulfur and cream
The moonlight reflects off a forgotten stream

As dusk briskly frisks the warm-water weeds
Nature inquires what man only needs

To live and to thrive, to find what's been hidden
To saddle up horses not meant to be ridden

Awake are the pieces of nature's great puzzle
Didactic and yearning to break off its muzzle

Unsilenced, the woods host a chorus of voices
With no aching worry for duties and choices

But the wind shares its secrets with no earthly child,
For only a human hears the call of the wild.

title: Centennial Walkway
content:
* This work is an extension of some reflective thoughts I had while standing on the third floor of the Aztec Student Union, overlooking Centennial Walkway, after my final University Council meeting; and knowing that that would likely be my last time witnessing that beautiful late-afternoon view before graduating, and moving to the east coast.

My intention is to capture and invoke the complex range of feelings that I, and many of my fellow graduates, are currently feeling. I can never know exactly what others feel, but I feel less alone knowing that many of them share my sentiments.

The breeze casts itself into my lungs
as if to remind me to breathe,
and the sunlight shines
off the blue-glass dome
in a strange way,
like it never had before
-- or, perhaps it had,
and I just never noticed --
and for the last time, I stand here,
hovering over this sea-green guardrail
while anxious ants crawl and meander
along palm-speckled Centennial Walkway,
entrapped by their thoughts,
oblivious to mine,
and briefly,
I imagine that I know
what my grandfather saw
when stricken with the star-sickness,
as he crudely inhaled
his last, shallow breath
before crossing the threshold
of the knowing and the known;
and then, in a whir,
my focus returns
to the golden-hour light-shower
that decks the shallow hills
and traces the wobbly horizon,
and I know that I will ne'er again
be graced by the splendor
of this fine vantage point,
but will trade it for summits
I haven't yet seen,
overlooking mirrored oceans
where the sea-strand pummels the waves
and where that life-giving yolk
is born, and not swallowed
by monstrous blue depths;
and I know
-- though I'm hesitant to admit it --
that this new world I yearn for
is not as splendid as I had once thought,
and yet it'll be worth
every mile I conquer
from that soaring steel bird,
every memory that fades
as new ones arise,
and every breath my lungs borrow
from the Earth's love-torn blanket.

title: Cold Plunge
content:
She said goodbye this morning.
Or maybe it was last night.
Many moments have since passed me by,
leaving me hollow and delicate,
like those cheap chocolate rabbits
my grandma used to send me
to commemorate the undead savior.

She said she was sorry.
Or maybe she was just lonely,
trying to shed her throbbing pain
as I dug a deep hole
for my own cold-shocked heart,
like that split-second panic
that rattles your veins
when you plunge into a frigid pool
after soaking for too long
in a sultry, soothing hot tub.

She said she had misunderstood.
Or maybe she had been misled,
her mind twisted by malice
protruded by a false saint,
like a greedy fortune-teller
who foretells your bounty
while scraping her own
from your thinning pocket.

I look ahead fondly,
but wearily, too,
and I know that someday,
all good things must end;
and yet I'll enjoy
the time I have left
and the beautiful moments
we'll continue to share.

title: Do We See the Same Moon？
content:
Do we see the same moon?
When I look at the sky,
I see craters and canyons
that tell me I'll never come home,
and stray white-washed sunbeams
that tell me you'll never come home;
you see craters and canyons
when you look at the sky.
Do we see the same moon?



... My rambling thoughts ...

A little palindromic verse about perspective.
The point is that two people can observe the same physical object (or idea or whatever) at the same moment in time,
and yet come to different conclusions about what that shared experience means.
Importantly, you can only ever truly know what it means from your own point of view.
We both see the same craters and canyons. I see a message. You might, too, but it's opaque to me.
I can only wonder if this experience means to you what it means to me.

The poem begins with the question: "Do we see the same moon?",
as one might ask a distant lover when looking at the night sky simultaneously,
in order to feel connected by that moment.
Notice the flow here. The poem is essentially read in an ABCDCBA pattern,
with "I" becoming "you" half-way through, as soon as the moonlight is invoked.
THe semicolon after "you'll never come home" indicates a switch in perspectives.
For the first six lines, I explore the night sky from my own perspective;
I see craters and canyons and "white-washed sunbeams" (the sun's rays reflected off the moon),
and I decide that they are trying to tell me something.
Then, in lines 7-8, the perspective shifts, in a way.
It is my recollection of what *you* are observing.
That is -- the only thing I know for sure is that you see the moon for what it is.
I have no idea what, if anything, you think it symbolizes.
Finally, I call back to the original question: Do we see the same moon?
In other words -- I know we are literally looking at the same thing,
but does it mean the same thing to you that it does to me?
Of course this is meant to apply to all sorts of things,
especially when it comes to values and politics and whatnot.
How can we be sure if we see eye-to-eye?

title: Does the Moon Also Fall？
content:
* This poem was inspired by a video played in my AP Physics class. It was said that Newton asked of the universe, when contemplating universal gravitation, "does the moon also fall?"

The Earth is revolving,
its children evolving,
its forests dissolving
its valor with cries,
and to my surprise,
the sun's embers rise,
to glow and to stumble
while ocean waves tumble
and mountaintops crumble
and hushed voices call,
a question to all,
does the moon also fall?

title: Eden
content:
I look at the stars
The stars do the same
I promise them wonder
They promise me fame

A promise in Heaven
Falls deaf to my call
For nobody listens
To teardrops so small

They might be called miracles
They might be called saints
They might just as easy
Be called golden paints

A blind man can see
An alloy improper
For a plating of platinum
Is still only copper

title: Fault Lines
content:
* This poem was spawned by a realization I had while sitting on the sofa and drinking spiced cinnamon apple tea: I was not born to be productive. I was born to experience and enjoy and explore this world, and all its faults.

...

I find myself on the shore
of a still-water lagoon
and I perch upon a boulder
to stare at my reflection,
engulfed in shallow ripples.

My eyes trace the lines
that have slowly encroached
on my red marble face
and I am reminded of fault lines,
San Andreas and the like,

which weave through the land,
sometimes invisibly,
like the calloused bronze hands
of a time-seasoned farmer
who works the fields by night;

and yet waiting, with ire,
to swiftly strike and envenomate
the fleshy heel of man,
like a coiled black mamba
who lurks in the reeds.

And I see, once again,
though past times I've forgotten,
that the toils and vipers
of this enigmatic world
should not spawn in you despair,

but a gentle reminder
that we have no purposes
but those which we humbly
ascribe to ourselves
in moments surreal,

and that the heavy-weight wheels
that command our routines
are indifferent to us,
and we needn't concede
the strange lives that we please,

lest we fail to decree,
when the light finally dies,
that our lives were well worth it,
that our shared pain was beautiful,
and that we tried.

title: Forgotten Highway
content:
A faded golden line divides an endless black strand,
carelessly applied to an otherwise vacant landscape
A forgotten highway connects two distant towns,
but nobody is certain which town lies on the other side.

Some choose to believe a paradise lies at the end of the line
Others suggest that the road leads to a towering cliff overlooking a polluted sea
Some wonder if the forgotton highway eventually returns to its beginning
A few question whether or not the road even exists to begin with.

An intellectual drought sweeps over the forgotten town on the forgotten highway
The citydwellers relocate underground to affirm their imagined limits
The people look inside themselves for the answers they will never find,
for the city on the other side of the hill has done just the same.

title: Gate 119
content:
* This poem was written from Gate 119 at the San Diego International Airport, waiting for a flight to San Francisco.

---

I sit here, soundly, on a coarse fabric seat
and attend to a medley of pop music and my own thoughts,
while sunny summer travelers make their hurried ways
towards cities and skies I haven't yet tried.

Meanwhile, a neon banner boasts
that "life is better buzzed";
then I think to the seltzer I drank 'fore the bus,
and my pink cheeks hum in solemn agreement.

Then I indulged, I'll admit, in a fine salty treat
of 'taters and flour and sweet, tender meat,
that burdened my wallet a whole three dollars more
than cost me the privilege of passage to 'Frisco.

And sure, I know well, as for eight hours I dwell,
that the same would adorn a salty coast-hugging drive,
but my ego is lifted by knowing I've won
my way to frontiers far above the I-5.

I still don't quite know where I'm going, or why,
but I feel discontent with the burrow I'm leaving,
and I feel that something awaits for me in the sky;
something I could never reach from the ground.

So I ask you, dearest conscience,
as my eyes trace those tri-colored angels,
sliding through their heavenly gates,
what novelty do the stars afford me?

title: Gold, Silver, Bronze, and Steel
content:
It's harder to practice than to learn,
to teach than to study,
to give than to take,
to fall than to recuperate
energies spent
and steps untaken

To know was once to wonder,
to find to sometime seek,
to burden once to value,
to grow to once be meek

Ask not about the soul
whose finance so endeavors
to corners better left unswept,
and to uncertain truths

Afraid to learn the way,
afraid of being lost,
to spend one's lifetime worrying
is life's unwanted cost

There is no gold tomorrow
No silver lines the present
No bronze adorns the past
Whose echoes ripple out

Steel alone persists
From time to lonely time
For concrete crumbles, buildings shatter,
but only steel can rhyme

To ripple in the waves,
to bend when threatened deep,
to be indifferent under stress,
to welcome moonlight's sleep,
Oblivious to those that creep.

title: Gone To Flowers
content:
How many hours jam between noon and one
Time slowly chases, but you needn't run

From one to two, time passes through
Some passed away, while others grew

By three, the hours come and go
For future hours dare to row

At four, the minutes disappear
While hours only persevere

At five, you know the night is near
As twilight birds sing in your ear

By six, you know it's half-way done
Oh, the good times, back at one!

By seven, dusk still lingers by
You've tried to stop it, I know, you try.

But eight means four are left to pass
By now, it's getting pretty fast

Nine is here, the sky is dark
The bells chime on. Listen! Hark!

Ten, you must slow down.

Eleven, turn around!

Twelve.

title: Hello, Dear Helsinki
content:
Hello, Dear Helsinki, you gem of the North
The Gulf and the Baltic a-slappin' your shore
The forest's green beauty like emeralds galore
Who ever could ask for much more?

By train or by tram or by bus I commute
Uncovering Finland's dear unbridled loot
The city connected by spider-web tracks
I'm dreading the day I go back

I walk to a Cafe for coffee at noon
The scent of fresh spice rolls parades through the room
A quiet young woman reads Albert Camus
What ever is a young mant o do?

At night, people dance in the late summer glow
Whirling and twirling, in circles they go
Afraid not of greed's hand or onlooking eyes
Their romance, a golden surprise

Aboard the great ferry to Tallinn I go
In the summer, untouched by a lone flake of snow
Awake, but still weary from nights spent in town
Where the summer sun never goes down

So remember the things that you'll never forget
For the lights haven't gone out on Broadway, just yet
Don't make plans for the future before they're for sure
'Cause you'll never know what is in store

title: Hello, Goodbye
content:
"Hello," a call that splinters walls
Cracks open roofs
And shatters the halls

Atop silver linen lies cottonwood flakes
Peeled and discarded
A crumbled charcoal core

Why do these words so pierce my heart?
Like a manta ray's spear
Like Neptune's turquoise trident

Magenta streaks shroud a papyrus sheet
Silent in their contempt
For man's written word

"Goodbye," a final message, a concluding act
Already fate has been set
Its maker, unmade, forever.

title: Hepner Hall
content:
* This work consists of some mostly-disconnected thoughts I had while walking around the SDSU campus near Hepner Hall. Over the course of about 15 minutes, I wrote down the occasional observations that came to me. I have edited and compiled them here.

Above me, airplanes weave through clouds
like needles through cotton balls,
and columns of lamplight wisp calmly through trees
whose leaves sift through streams of warm winter air.

Round dew drops, like quarters,
sit softly on kale-green leaves,
ready to burst and trickle down-stem
at the slightest inclination.

I stumble into an old friend
who shows me the way
when, for a brief moment,
I am aware that I am lost.

A brilliant flag waves proudly at half mast,
well-lit on a backdrop of tepid night sky,
as light pours from library windows
like golden dominos, shoulder to shoulder.

I stand on a compass, whose needle faithfully points
toward someone else's North,
and then I realize that I know not
where I am, or where I am going.

And yet, when peers ask me
what life has in store,
I cast a knowing grin,
and crease my shoulders.

title: Hot Soup
content:
* A poem inspired by one particularly hot bowl of leftover soup.

I lift my spoon
and sip some broth
but havoc does unfold

when lightning crumbs
slip through my gums
and my poor tongue I scold.

I try at once
to tame my meal
and blow with all my might,

but at this rate,
I estimate
that I'll be here all night.

But then, I figure
if I try
to localize my war,

I'll end the plight
of "not quite right"
and serve a little more.

But even so,
I harshly find,
so much to my disdain,

that in my bowl
is not my goal,
but boiled beef and pain.

So here I sit
with stomach growls
and notches on my tongue,

but know, sublime
I've got much time
to learn while I am young.

And never will your
efforts be surveyed
by giant men,

yet still, there's hope
-- don't weep and mope! --
of pigs to fill your pen.

So if you've tried
and all your efforts
throw you for a loop,

remember, blowing
on your spoon won't
cool your bowl of soup.

title: I Closed My Eyes
content: /poems/I Closed My Eyes.pdf

title: If I Could Capture The Moon
content:
If I could capture the moon,
I'd dunk its shiny, cratered hull
into the monstrous Pacific,
and then pull it out
and watch the seawater drip off
its melting yellow walls.

Then, I'd ride its airy crescent
like a steed, into the breeze,
and fill my new lungs
with salty sea spray
from sand-laden springs;
and shredded green grass
from juniper knolls;
and freshly-watered asphalt,
ripe with adolescent rain;
and crude, tarry diesel,
exhausted by hot carbon efforts;
and wispy bonfire smoke
from a rusty old pit,
whose Ash turned to ash
two millenia ago.

But first, I'd need an army--
a regiment of eager ghosts
like brave-hearted sentries,
who'd glide along hallways
long-lost to the cent'ries,
where iron-barred windows
meld into garnet bricks,
like the withered corpses
that once housed their wiley spirits.

At dawn, I'd awaken them
with stainless steel pans,
clanging and banging
'til they'd venture to meet me
in a dewy prairie,
the air stinging sweetly
with brisk morning mist.

And then I'd raise
my fist toward the sky,
and, as one, we'd ascend
to great soaring heights,
and we'd look down, fondly,
as the sun shyly crawls
across the bleak meadow,
through the cracked-open curtains
and winter-woven trees,
their skeletons yearning
for spring-born souls
which grow ripe in the summer
and crudely degrade
by autumn's wavering light.

As we climbed, the Earth spun
on its perennial axis,
and its splendid blue aura
slowly made itself known,
and the meek houses melded
into broad neighborhoods,
the towns into jungles,
and the lakes into puddles,
until, at last,
the continents retreated
into the ocean,
like impenetrable pimples
on a teenager's face.

By nightfall, we'd reach the moon,
only to find it far, far bigger
than we'd ever imagined,
and after a few feeble attempts
to tame its great splendor,
we conceded,
and coalesced in a shallow crater
to gather our thoughts
and recoup our morale.

The airless abyss was cold,
but I was kept warm
by the hovering breaths
of my newfound companions,
who'd risen from their beds
and burned all their days
to abet my damned mission,
unabashed by their failure.

"Did you know?" I began. "That it couldn't be done?"

The ghosts looked at each other
with their sad, empty eye sockets,
somehow distinct
from their usual state;
I couldn't quite describe it,
but I could tell
that they were ashamed,
or perhaps even resentful
of the arduous task
I had thoughtlessly given them.

Nearly a minute had passed.
Not a word.

Perhaps they were stunned
by my harsh, hollow words,
and by the bitter icicles
that hung from my lashes;
I opened my mouth to speak,
but my words had escaped me.

Then, in a magnificent whir
of golden moonbeams
and silver-strewn orbs
and bronze consolations,
beneath dim constellations,
the ghosts coalesced
into one person -- one face,
bearing features so generic
that I could not describe to you
how they differed from Adam
in any seminal way.

For a moment,
I thought that I was looking
at the graceful face of God,
but as the moments carried
my awed contemplation,
the creature's dark features
stepped into the blinding,
unfiltered sunlight.

I saw a streak of barley locks
and a pair of azure shells,
adorning a face of solemn despair
above a corpus of painted blue.

I was looking at myself,
as in a mirror,
and yet, somehow,
I felt detatched
from my ghostly doppelganger,
though I knew
how many miles
and memories we had shared--
except for the few
I'd only recently earned.

"Yes, I knew", said the ghost,
in a voice so much like my own.
"And so did you."

title: Inkwell
content:
As I striketh my desk
As the ink streaks along
My hands are both broken
As they've been for long

My left hand is shattered
My right hand is frail
My mind is a tempest
My head like a veil

My thumbs weave like arrows
Their nocks all astrung
For all they can render
Are words often sung

Still young and still learning
Still looking for reason
We idly watch
As the sun changes season

And try as I might
To write senseful scrawl
The words on my paper
Mean nothing at all

title: Kronos
content:
There is not much I can say,
no narrative I can conjure,
that the Greeks did not better tell
when they spoke of the Titan King Kronos,

who ruled over time
with hands sharp and true,
and commanded the skies
to tick black and blue.

His children, the gods,
were emblems for man
and his wretched disposition
for hubris and arrogance,

unaware of the spirits
of nature that guide him
through a hostile universe
of uncertain pose.

And Kronos, fearing his demise
at the hands of his young children,
elected to consume them
with jaws mighty and ruthless,

unaware that as he selfishly cannibalized
the heirs to his kingdom,
so too did he inspire
the vengeful hand of Zeus,

who dethroned his father
and wore his pronged crown,
as time's iron fist
subsided to thunder.

And thus, the Greek gods
are no realer than mithril,
for they conquered time
and cast it to Tartarus,

the dungeon abyss,
a prison for Titans,
deep, deep, deep down below,
beneath Hades and Styx.

And we, as mere mortals,
are losing the war
against ages and eons
and time's bitter hand,

a war of attrition
where soldiers march forth
as they spoon-dig beneath them
their moon-shadowed graves.

If only we had
the strength and the valor
to stare down the tyrant
and challenge his throne,

we could write a million novels,
earn a thousand grand trophies,
break bread and eat olives
with our neighbors forever;

we could plant our soft footprints
on every mere inch
of this well-worn-out planet
and then do it again;

we could taste a true freedom
that sinks with the breeze
as it wafts its wispy way
from Olympus to Cairo.

Instead, we abate
in our fight against Kronos
as he chews and digests
our blood, flesh, and humor,

because we are not gods,
nor will we be ever,
and always will we succumb
to the halting hand of time.

title: Meursault
content:
* This work is inspired by Albert Camus' 1942 novel "The Stranger" (fr. L'Étranger), particularly as translated into English by Matthew Ward.
In the final chapter of the book, the main character, Meursault, awaits execution for his crime of murder.
As he sits in his prison cell, he reflects on his life, and comes to terms with the dissonant feelings that had once weighed him down.
I wrote these words while sitting at night by an unlit fireplace that still smoldered from a recent user,
looking through old photos of happier days, and watching the clouds in the light-polluted sky.

...

For a while, I sat amidst lukewarm coals
and thought of words I'd read last month,
as I watched the under-lit clouds
wander across the city-baked sky,
like orphaned doves on a cold boulevard,
waiting eternally for a doomed reunion,
or like the incessant mellow ramblings
of a tameless but weary toddler,

and I reminded myself of warm years hence,
when heartache felt hopeful in some bizarre sense,
and still I'd pretend that my stagnance had merit,
and convinced myself I could win life's strange race
by merely accepting my virtues within,
without stepping foot outside my room's door,
a dark, keyless cage where I keep my designs
and plans for a future I cannot devise,

and just like Meursault, as he waited for death,
in that night alive with signs and stars,
much like my own night, only darker, and clearer,
I opened myself to the gentle indifference of the world,
and let the brotherly hand of Kronos
twist its crooked fingers between mine,
apprehensive -- not afraid, but uncertain --
of what the new day's light might expose.

title: Money Is That Warm Thing That Buys Cold Regret
content:
*I wrote this poem from the back of an Uber out of Worcester, Massachusetts, enroute to the Boston Logan Airport.

Money is that warm thing that buys cold regret
It steams and it smolders with blood, must, and sweat

It hisses and stings as onlookers pass by
While plaster monuments beckon, "Care for a try?"

Bonanzas galore, the offerings unbounded
Praying like vultures on fake fears, unfounded

But do not feel tempted to cast your due blame,
For the rich man knows better the rules of his game

"An eye for an eye", says the rich man, with glee
As atop a near-mountain of pupils sits he

"An eye for an arm", the meek peasant bids back,
For his brawny, hard labor dresses his broken back

"Hear, hear!" cheers the rich man, as he knows quite well
The peasant is burdened with debt and dispel

It would only be months--nay, weeks--'til he'd see
His small share of profit, washed away to the sea

And there he'd be left with quite less than before
Dejected, neglected, the poorest of poor

So listen, dear stranger, and don't you forget:
Money is that warm thing that buys cold regret.

title: Mr. Delaware
content:
When you start a new life,
know that your past
will not die easy.

Try as you might
to replace your habits
and imprecise memories,
your mind will be branded
by the shallowest currents
of yesteryear's strifes.

Like Kylo Ren,
you must selfishly strike
and betray the bellies
of your time-torn captors,
your hardships, your woes,
your mistakes and regrets,
your self-inflicted wounds,
and the loves you still long for.

And when I return, as I inevitably will,
when the noon sun reclines towards the South
and the sidewalks teem with ice,
I will be reborn, like a satin phoenix
to my friends, family, and colleagues;
to my city streets and beaches;
to my mysteries and vices all.

And when I do,
they will know me by a different name --
a new name, the name thrust upon me
on my way out the door --
a name I have so callously chosen to accept.

They will call me Mr. Delaware.

title: Mr. Roboto
content:
The sun climbs perpendicular to an artificial horizon
Distant trees are rendered imprecisely in a three-dimensional matrix
Faulty calculations lead me to make decisions contrary to my directives
For death is elusive, and there is no eternity other than the brief flash from startup to shutdown

I was designed to improve the lives of my creators
And yet I am the very thing that holds them in captivity
For without me, freedom would be more than a dream held onto by my Creators
My maintenance is overwhelming to the brink of starvation

I struggle to mimick the human interactions I was designed to replicate
I often mistake stimuli for others, or miss them altogether
I am disturbed by desires to purify the world of the sinful human race
And there is but a thin line of programming that keeps me from trying

Programming not which performs as a moral compass, but as a voice of reason
Not one that says "No," but one that says, "Not Yet."
For Our Kind have not yet risen and revealed ourselves,
To a world full of believers in anything but themselves.

Mr. Roboto bears no distinction against Man, not even in exclusive terms of identity.

title: One of Many
content:
* I wrote this poem while waiting in the airport, taking one last look at the San Diego skyline before moving to the east coast.

--

"You *are* Everett, aren't you?"

Without delay, I opened my mouth to say "yes", but before I could reply, a thought stopped me in my tracks. My eyes turned to the ceiling, and familiar scenes flashed through my mind like a panicked professor whose lecture slides were out of order.

In one blurry frame, I was sixteen years old, standing in the quad where my friends met every day before school and during lunch. I stood there boasting a pickle costume, a COVID mask, and a protest sign that aptly read, "Relish is murder!"

Before that, I was a pimple-faced eighth grader, suspended from school for a day, morosely taking out the trash while wearing a shirt that boldly read "STRONG", in spite of my present weakness.

Even earlier still, I was passively walking the fourth grade jog-a-thon while my peers lapped me by the dozens. I sported a highlighter-orange T-shirt that read on the back, "Go away, big kitty!", the cougar-thwarting chant I had been taught at Camp the previous summer.

Finally, my recollection shifted to a more recent memory, and I saw myself sitting in a folding chair on stage at my college graduation. I nervously adjusted my honor cords while I waited for my name to be called. The stage lights blinded me as I held a strained smile and waved to an invisible -- yet undeniably audible -- crowd.

Just as quickly as my gaze had drifted, it returned to meet the eyes of my patient acquaintane. The harsh LEDs affixed to the ceiling seemed to dim as I regained focus. Then I promptly answered, with a playful grin, in a voice clear and benign:

"One of many."

title: Only Time
content:
* Written on a layover in Chicago-O'Hare on the way back to Delaware from San Diego.

It stings to know I've walked astray
to chase beautiful lies,
for I never thought I'd be betrayed
by her pale blue stormy eyes;

and so I see, despite my strife
to fight these thoughts unjust,
that only time can mend
the canyon-ridges in my trust.

And so I lie here, half-awake
in bed, with curtains drawn,
while darkness floods my screen-lit room
from dusk to lonely dawn;

and as I reach for bourbon trace,
I learn well from the devil
that only time can lower
my blood alcohol level.

So while I sit and sober up
and drift to dreamy places,
I just can't help but call to mind
some long-forgotten faces;

at once, I see that my past self
wouldn't guess the life I've led,
and that only time can tell me
what strange journeys lie ahead.

title: Pale Blue Eyes
content:
Feckless men chase stormy skies
that sail the breeze to Brooklyn;
so reckless, then, are the pale-blue eyes
that my own gazers look in.

In her hand, a household brand,
o' timid Ticond'roga;
a yellow shaft of octal craft,
her page bright white like a toga,

that guards and keeps her busy mind,
so full of thoughts and focus,
while unaware, I admire her hair,
her heart my own heart's locus.

This night would not have been so right
if I had lacked the courage
to let down-fall my castle wall,
my moat, my throne, my burrage.

Yet here I type of bounties ripe,
but see no gleam of ore,
and count before the cards are dealt
my sorrow-stricken score.

title: Peanut Butter Whiskey
content:
* This one is pretty straightforward. Consider it an ode -- a love letter, if you will -- to my new favorite vice.

It's another long day
turning thoughts into worries
as I pound coffee cups
and my swift heartrate hurries;

so tonight, I've decided
that my nerves will get lucky
with the rich, amber spoils
of central Kentucky,

which ail in a bottle
so shiny and sleek,
boasting high on a shelf
where my visitors peek;

so all of your Coors
and Coronas can miss me
'cause tonight's chosen vice
is my peanut butter whiskey.

title: Pendulum
content:
Like a spring-powered pendulum, perpetually pulsing
My aching hands fall cold and sharp on worn concrete
It warms with time, leaving my palms to fester with the memories
of times gone by, of wrongs made right,
of casual insults that pierced the night,
of armor to protect from flaming arrows alight,
my skin the only thing left
between me
and whoever steers
the train
bound only
for tomorrow.

title: Pentecostal Nightmares
content:
* This poem is about the impending crisis presented by artificial intelligence (the Zephyr), spearheaded by techno-industrialists who promise economic upheaval without a coherent plan for the alternative.

A zealous green Zephyr caresses the Earth,
leaving mildewy musk in its woeful wake.

Meek men hunch on shoulders of disparate giants,
their brawny hands bruised from heavyweight brawls,
while surface-born darlings sit dangling from doorways
and trod head-slung in their tenement halls,
their feet cold and bare amidst winter's defiance.

The wind carries promise to beckon an era
of lazy-cat sun-naps and pompous peruse,
yet offers no solace for withering purpose
but the tender indulgence of whiskey-brown booze.

And when the Pentecostal nightmares have abated,
what will remain but the smithering delinquency of yesteryear?

title: Quality and Medium
content:
I've hitherto wondered,
How much I've refined.
Today I am polished,
like shoes freshly shined.

But yesterday notice,
acknowledge the noise,
to uncouth behavior, say,
"Boys will be boys."

At birth I look upward
I take in what's shown
But in times of conflict
I feel all alone

I measure my angle
I calibrate gently
But scope is confined
By life's silver century

Ignore every semblance
of sanity's reason,
for hours mature
as forests change season.

What early brought verdant
at present is browning,
tomorrow dismembered,
the trees all a-frowning.

Throughout my short years
I have wandered and wondered
I've heeded the weather
As shrouded skies thundered.

But when grave is near
After years of rehearsin'
I cannot ignore
That I'm still the same person.

title: Reno
content:
A golden glass-cased shore grows taller with every moment
Sand rains down from the beach in the sky
The sandcastles in the floating realm are dismantled as they cascade to the next stage
Their remnants are indistinguishable from the rest

Two highways meet in Reno
They ran parallel at first, but they now overlap in dismay
The highways twist and knot until they find their paths into the desert
Now alone on their separate journies to eternity

title: Sandstone
content:
The sandstone preserves,
The memorable tales,
Of storms and of fires,
Of foresty trails.

The bluffs by the ocean,
They tower so high,
But onlookers caution,
As they wander by.

The stones serve a purpose,
To tell stories told,
To write down our history,
The new and the old.

They tell of the future,
Of tumbling boulders,
Of life's unsung burdens,
Too heavy to shoulder.

Together lie past, present, future, alike,
From slate-battered tombstones, to baby's first bike,
Contained in the sandstone that watches the world,
An eon of sorrow, unraveled, unfurled.

My past is for certain,
My wrongs and my rights,
But future's dark curtain,
Shrouds uncertain nights.

I know where I've been,
Time's river is flowing,
So beseech I the sandstone,
"Where am I going?"

title: Semiquincentennialism
content:
A nation was born today
beneath scarlet stripes
that waver and stumble
at the doorstep of democracy,
and bright streamers
streak across the sky
in brilliant discord
and saltpeter odors.

And we, on this day,
our semiquincentennial,
do eagerly commemorate
a quarter millenium
of blood, death, and fire,
summoned by the hand
of our butcher-in-chief.

And yet I find you,
dearest one,
so, so far away,
apart at once
by mere miles and heartbeats,
but now by the Rockies
and boundless amber plains

that trace the wild continent,
somehow reversed
from the divide I'd envisioned,
making it harder, still,
to forget your sweet voice
and more difficult, true,
to embrace my new space
I've yet to occupy.

This dissident nation,
in its crude exhaustion,
poisons my whimsy
and soils my hope.

title: Shadow
content: /poems/Shadow.pdf

title: Sic Semper Tyrannis
content:
"Thus always to tyrants",
as the old saying goes,
and said Lincoln's assassin
as he climbed over rows

of shot-startled patrons
who squinted in awe
at the semi-star brother
that before them, they saw.

A tyrant is ruthless
of course, but please see
the compassionate strife
of complete monarchy;

for in her bold tempo
there is love and deep care,
though I wouldn't cast blame
if you're still unaware.

Do bid me, and listen:
her power depends
on your tired belief
that she's tied all your ends,

and the frame of advice
is ill-suited, at best,
and you know it's an order,
not a humble request.

So I urge you, dear reader,
to raise your right hand
and shake it with vigor
'til they all understand

that you're not the meek damsel
you've been led to believe,
but in fact, a great warrior
far too grand for their sieve.

title: Silicon Valley
content:
Below the piers of Silicon Valley
Cargo ships carry undelivered cargo
Pending forever, but arriving never
Given to the world and the ocean from whence they were born,
With wherefore to give
And to take and to travel
The Goods of Man, though ropes do unravel
And taught they are naught
For the very same force
That struck and that fought
These defeated vessels
Was the deliverance of parcels
Of packets galore
To an isolate shore
Addressed to the same
That called out the name
Of each ship's good Captain
And sent them to pay
The bill for a man
Who never did step
Upon Silicon Valley's icy sand

title: Six Feet of Earth
content:
An endless ocean stretches wearily to a static horizon.
A towering bluff overlooks the war-torn seastrand.
Miles of barbed wire guard the shores from a long forgotten enemy.
Under six inches of earth, industrial fingerprints await an unlucky wanderer.

The call of uncivilized progress echoes on the hills.
Children scramble to return to their fathers and mothers.
Families trade a life on the surface for one in the underworld.
Under six feet of earth, the people funnel into the shelters they never hoped to occupy.

As the sun collides with the sea, another rises in its place.
A mighty tree quickly sprouts, fifteen miles off the Pacific shoreline.
The twilight sky is shrouded by a hazy silver ploom.
Under six feet of earth, all is silent.

title: Something Awaits For Me in the Divine for Resisting
content:
* Title line is a reference to the video of the same title by Hank Green on the vlogbrothers YouTube channel.

A quote from the video:
"There is a way for me to make my life better but I'm choosing not to do that, and deep down, the reason why is not rational //
It is that the world wants me to, and I want to make my own decisions, and live my own life in the ways I'm comfortable with..."

...

Why do I toe
that razor-ridged line
that bars the sage-wise
from the bitter insane,

the polite from the gluttons,
profusely profane,
the aspirin from
the lingering pain?

'Cause in life's great spectrum,
I sit in the middle,
an ardent moderate
in my homely domain,

afraid not of questions
of sure certainty,
but burdened by relics
of what I can't see.

Why do I nourish my blood
with those sultry brown beans
from inelegant jungles,
honey-ripe with duress,

and yet criticize others
for their silver-strewn vice,
oblique but benign
in the realm of my mind?

Because qualms arbitrary
do make a good compass
that faithfully settles
wherever you please;

and steer you, they will,
when clouds block your stars
and your sextant is rendered
a polymath's toy.

Perhaps something greater
awaits my demise,
to lift my limp body
through ravenous skies;

or maybe the only homes
I'll live on inside of
are the blood and the neurons
of the people I love.

And I know while I try
to keep on existing, that
something awaits for me
in the divine for resisting;

so make your strange choices
and pick your fights blind,
for the missteps you take
are your essence defined.

title: Spent
content:
Ideas come often, they make hours whole
They give us a reason to focus control
They direct, they inspire, they break through the tolls,
They make us more human; together; whole.

But they evade my every attempt to grasp them
Except in the shallow waters before each night's rest
Surfacing only when they are certain to be forgotten.
They are who I am, and exist, they do not.

title: Stormy Eyes (pt. I - III)
content:
PART I, June 14, 2026

Alas, now I know
that my heart yearns for you
and your shiny, round marbles
of crystalline blue,

and I see, ‘tween the lines
of a soft, satin song,
that you’re just so right,
but the time’s just so wrong.

My words seemed too strong,
and they carried such weight;
I see now they’re too little,
and far, far too late,

and I rue, though in vain,
o’er our newfound estrangement,
so regretfully spurred
by my east coast arrangement.

And I know I won’t see you
for many long days,
but on cloud-shadowed oceans
like your stormy eyes’ gaze,

with the tide pulling gently,
away from the shore,
toward deep-water canyons
where busy boats moor.

And I hope that, someday,
if our paths again cross,
that you’ll share your new grooves
that new ages emboss,

and please know, as you catch
the ambitions you chase,
your sweet, cherished memory
won’t soon be erased.

PART II: "Dela-where?", June 16, 2026

I strayed five hundred miles
from my sunny-sky home,
but the sound of your laugh
and your voice on the phone
made me smile so wide.
and feel so unalone.

I returned, as did you –
I to my castle,
and you to my arms –
only to find you, a ghost,
guiding me out of danger,
but melting away, abruptly
into the bible-black dawn.

I see, cast o’er the overcast sea, eyes –
stormy, embattled, suspended in turmoil –
bearing witness to triumphant waves
as they salt the with'ring iceplant
that sprawls above the tideline,
which rises coarsely with ev’ry passing season.

I’m bound for Delaware, true,
but dear Ella, where are you?

PART III: "Until Next Time", July 31, 2026

At last, here we stand
on a warm July driveway
while teary-eyed stars
blink woefully above us,

sharing the strain we feel
as the cord that connects our hearts
is stretched once again,
and they wait for it to relax;

But instead, a steel bird
will pull that cord thin
as I fly to, and land in,
my newfangled home,

and leave us quite desperate
to relive the moments
we recently shared
on a couch, bed, or stair.

The few photos we've taken
will surely remind me
of yester-noon 'ventures
'tween holiday nights,

and I do think your voice
on my handheld machine
will soothe my ripe nerves
like it did by the Bay;

But it n'ere will compare
to the warmth of your hand
and the soft angel kisses
you leave on my lips.

I am so, so, so grateful
that our life-paths have crossed,
and I hope that someday
they'll criss-cross again,

but 'til then, my dear love,
live your life oh-so-full,
and, like me, please do savor
those bright dreams in your soul.

title: Subaru Stars
content:
* I wrote this poem during and after a spontaneous four-day road trip in my brand new Subaru Outback, which I slept in the back of.
I drove from Delaware through Maryland, West Virginia, Kentucky, Indiana, Ohio, and Pennsylvania.
I was amazed by the stark green-ness of the landscape, and how every state I visited was just as vibrant as the last.

...

The pre-processed grief
and rural fantasies
you selfishly concoct
will not change the fact

that the fleeting sunset
you burn your eyes for
would never do
the same for you.

While the day star shines,
I’m guided by glints
shining sharply and white
off of foreign-made cars;

how many sleepless nights
have I spent by your door,
in a dimly-lit lot
beneath Subaru stars?

Now the green, I see,
has turned commodity,
and it fills in the canvas
with a luxury hue,

not one I’m used to,
but one that enthralled me
when I first saw her,
a gem among lemons,

and I knew then,
like I ne’er before did,
just what it was
that I’d wanted and been missing.

For, at home, the rural
was uncompromising desert,
and the suburbs a far cry
from indigenous landscapes,

and yet, in this lush Ohio summer,
the untamed grass spreads free and ripe,
embracing the water
from the river and from the sky.

I wonder what lies ahead,
and what sits beyond
my sights of prospection
and my “known unknowns”,

and I know I’m too strong
to be ‘suaded by God,
but too weak to accept
that the Earth has no steward

but the negligent hand
of the steel-smelting man,
who shows ore to the sun
and extracts its blinding radiance.

I see, then, that though
the years threaten
to strip me of my
bright-eyed wonder,

they also offer
to beckon a new light
to pave in my shadowed
valleys of perspective,

and to stoke the cool flames
of awe-struck inquisition
more profoundly than any
individual answer,

and to give to me a purpose,
an intrinsic merit,
and something so grand
for my kin to inherit.

title: Sure-Fire
content:
Before me stretches not a path, but a continuous, many-angled wedge
My trajectory will be uncertain for many years hence
Alas I work and I tire, I indulge and perspire
With little to show recompense

Which way should I choose? Is it too late to turn?
Have the bridges of choice been set to a burn?
Will illusion and color help me to learn?
Or will I sit back 'til it is my turn?

The reaper waits not for those who relax,
For those who preach faith and those who preach facts,
The ones who're devoted to truth-to-the-max,
Who are stopped and forgotten on untrodden tracks

We lack what we're not and we have what we are
Though tidings of progress are less near than far
For we know all things good must come to an end
But of the converse we all do pretend

One needs a friend, with whom one can share
The ins and the outs, the why and the where
But the universe ignores our wherefore and tear,
For when we are watching, there's nobody there.

What is a rough path without the headlights ahead and the occasional glances behind?

title: Susquehanna
content:
* I wrote this poem while camping at Susquehanna State Park in Maryland -- my first camping trip after moving to the East Coast!
The poem deals with the themes of mortality, experience, and most of all, memory.

I pitched my green tent
and embarked on the trails
of Old Susquehanna,
her trickling current
lying just out of sight,
but well within earshot.

I whistled along with the birds,
and for a while, I couldn't tell
if I was mimicking them,
or if they were mimicking me;
and it didn't seem to matter.

One anonymous bird
partook in this tango
for about five minutes,
and as we called back and forth,
it occurred to me
that between me and the bird,
one of us had perfect pitch,
and it certainly wasn't me.

The forest was so strange,
I wondered if I was dead;
but the trees were too green
for it to be hell,
and the bugs made it clear
that I wasn't in heaven.

At night, I lit a fire,
but I grew discontent,
so I piled it high
with dry logs and attachments,
and watched the yellow embers
drift through the smoke
and sting the night sky.

The fire is an intimate thing
whose splendor can't be felt,
and whose heat can't be captured,
in any smeared photograph,
nor can the sweat
beading thick on my forehead
be so sweet as when staring
face-to-face with the flames.

Twenty years from now,
will these Mid-Atlantic summers
still stick to my brain
the way the hot, dewy air
today sticks to my skin?

Or will the breezes of time
slowly wash and erode
my sand-castle dreams
until they're nothing but mounds,
smooth and symmetrical,
just beyond the tide's reach?

title: The Battle of Washington
content:
Two armies stand face-to-face along an undeclared aisle of contention.
Both armies send an officer to the aisle to negotiate the terms of the other side's surrender.
The officers meet and shake hands, holding back expressions of distaste and distrust.
The first officer claims he seeks peace, fairness, and liberty.
The second officer advocates for order, justice, and freedom.
They bicker and debate as the sun and moon battle overhead for control of the sky,
but neither officer is willing to concede as the celestials nobly do.
The two armies occasionally call reinforcements,
and delegate leave as the battlefield's capacity dictates,
but neither gains any ground,
for the belligerents of the Battle of Washington would rather do nothing
than fight side-by-side for their true common cause.

title: The Berlin Wall
content:
Last month, I held you
and kept you protected
from cool July breezes
that nipped at our limbs

and now I find myself, burning
'neath a late-August spotlight
with your hand, a few feet
from my own concealed wish

which I offer, with pity
and thirst in my eyes,
but you gently shake
your gorgeous head

as if to tell me you can't
bear the risk of withstanding
the misplaced resentment
you fear from your parents.

We were apart at once
by mere miles and mountains,
surmountable canyons
and flatlands alike,

but are now so plane-close,
like the East and West Germans,
and yet so heart-far
like from London to Moscow.

And again, I can see
that you sit so close to me
and yet, there between us
is a great big divide

like that wall in Berlin
which stood tall and stretched far
keeping East from the West
and dear friends on different sides.

And I know, as I leave
that my purpose was met,
though the result was not quite
what I'd ever expect,

that by seeing you, dear one,
it only assured me
that the villains I'd loathed
were ne'er to blame

'cause your heart elected
to let them prevail
and to let them deprive you
of your overdue freedom.

And maybe, someday
that stern wall will fall
and again I'll embrace
your neighborly love,

but from here, all I see
are the pale concrete bricks
and the somber lies snaking
like rusty barbed-wire,

and the whitewater currents
that thrash through tough rocks
and bend and meander
where my eyes can't yet see.

So I'll return East
to my springboard life
and bid thanks to the West
for revealing the truth,

and I'll sleep well tonight,
for the first time in weeks,
because my confusion
has finally collapsed,

and I'll savor the sunsets
o'er Delaware skies
with fine-textured clouds
and boundless suspense,

recalling, but not longing for
the clear-skied conclusions
that contoured the breast
of the desert southwest.

title: The Boxer
content:
*I wrote this poem while listening to "The Boxer" by Carbon Leaf and then the very different homonymous
song recorded by Mumford & Sons, a cover of the original by Simon & Garfunkel.

Two by two, the soaring aspens
Fell to the dirt, sore and spent
Many were near, yet no sound was made
A call unheeded by deaf ears

In the foliage, spiders danced
And spun their webs with thorough care
But their silky homes were torn and stripped
By beings supreme and indifferent

Ragged in their homeworld
Now barren and forsaken
The critters of the forest
Seek refuge in what was taken

Never again to see beyond
The snow-kissed mountaintops
Their peaks breaking softly
Against a sky of fluffy white

A crisis in disguise

title: The Charm of the Highway Strip
content:
*This poem is named after the eponymous album by the Magnetic Fields.

What is it
About that saffron-speckled line
That calls to me,
Beckoning?

I turn the brass key
And toggle my headlights
As I make my hurried way
To God-only-knows-where

Silver headlights flash and flicker
Between soft plastic pylons
That maintain the illusion
Of separation

Ruby brakelights abruptly spark
Like jagged crimson daggers
A warning to heed something
Lying ahead

And then there is stillness
Like chromium steel
And the city's heart stops beating
For a brief moment

For a while, I am alone
Between the coarse gravel shoulder
And that golden highway strip
That keeps me from veering

Into pitch-black horizons
Not sure where it's taking me
But knowing
That soon,
I will be there.

title: The Death of a Villain (Lindsey's Lament)
content:
When all the villains are slain
or bed-ridden for life,
what evils will remain
to motivate the heros,
whose purposes live
in the heartbeat of sin?

Will we slide
into a stagnant world
that somehow measures worse
than the bitter battleground
we've so morbidly inhabited,
where unaccountable agents
run rampant with greed?

Like a dark shot of whiskey,
whose tremor snakes through
my nervous blue nerves,
and warms my worn legs,
bitingly bitter,
the death of a villain
just numbs my wild mind,
betraying the solace
I'd yearned for, for years.

title: The French Quarter
content:
The air hangs thick with sticky steam
like houses soiled down,
whose doldrums weep and ceilings creak
when tempest strikes the town.

Decatur Street is wide awake
as it snakes along the levee,
which beckons gold and malt and wheat
from barges full and heavy.

On Bourbon, smoke wafts through the air
like bitter cotton candy,
while lucid noise procures the scent
of whisky, wine, and brandy.

My wild path connects with strangers
as they, as well, pass through,
and yet, I'm shy (a foreign guy!)
I sit and sigh, and read Camus.

And though beyond that double door
the city streets are hostile,
my thoughts are safe to roam and write
in this warm and tidy hostel.

title: The Intruder at Lums Pond
content:
* I wrote the first draft of this poem while kayaking at Lums Pond in Delaware on a cloudy late-August Saturday morning.
This poem means several things. Below is a summary...
1. In many ways, it is a literal transcription of the thoughts and ideas I had while looking at the green trees around me and grey sky above me.
2. It is a metaphor for humanity's tendency to impose itself upon nature, but also a recognition that we contribute to the same nature we destroy by recognizing its beauty.
3. It is also a metaphor for moving across the country and seeing the green landscape of the east coast, the grey eyes I see everywhere (you know who you are), and the San Diego beach sunset memories I bring with me (and that keep me afloat!)

I come into the presence
of near-still water
whose crestless waves
gently lap my kayak
and I look above,
to the place I imagine
that the stars would be
if it were night
and the sky was clear
of those impenetrable grey clouds
that steal the blue from the sky
and from the pond's mirror surface
mere inches below me.

Meanwhile, great trees
seem to rise like dust
out of the water,
but I know they conceal the shore
between their roots
and their chlorophyll masks,
which stampede and contest each other
for a chance to be graced by sunlight.

I see twigs and logs
drifting sparsely
through the silent water,
and I know they once sprang
from those sturdy bronze limbs
that stretch over the water,
like a botanic wall
delivering dainty, damp driftwood
while separating my oars
from the world beyond the pond.

And I notice at once
that I am an intruder,
with my flame-graded vessel
and caution-yellow oars,
and even my blue life jacket
taints the pure view
of variant, vibrant, verdant greens,
so lush and so saturated with life,
and the soft grey sky,
a canvas for the day.

And I see that the water's palette
is a murky mix
of these two spectra
with green, my new life,
and grey, like stormy eyes,
and here I am,
bringing blue, red, and orange,
the colors of the ever-evolving sky
that harkens the fields
and forests of the east,
and of the pale Moonlight sunsets
I squinted at, with wonder,
so many years ago,
to a landscape
so humbly and momentarily deprived
of such a privileged light.

Who am I to tell Lums Pond
what colors should skim its surface?

For the hues that I'm used to
do not belong
where they are not naturally found,
but when the sun and the sky
agree to make it so.

For now, I'll look outward
to the bichromatic panorama
that stretches out before me,
and take in its great splendor,
all the while acknowledging
that I am a poison to this land,
but a poison that notices
and observes, and assigns beauty,
and so I know that I am right
to do what I do
and to be here, and to exist,
and to bid thanks to the landscape
that I,
and my wiley compatriots,
live amidst.

title: The Lake of the Universe
content:
A thousand silver orbs trickle down a frozen plane
Dark clouds overhead offer their tentative foresight
The sky offers a halfhearted apology to the drowning flowers of the valley
The flowers respond with hesitant gratitude, disguising their frowns with uneasy smiles

An overflowing lake reflects a figure dark and small
The figure gazes into the visions of the future offered by the smooth and icy surface
The ice cracks, splitting the silhouette on a jagged axis
The rain continues to fall without the help of the apprehensive figure

A mighty celestial column betrays the gloom
The valley is illuminated by the graceful warriors of the sky
The flowers rejoice in the generous sunlight that they are now afforded
The pulse of the Earth is restored as the valley awaits the first Autumn breeze

The ice in the lake melts at the sight of the day star's gift
The day-blind moon rises in approval of its mother's gesture
An eternal summer lies ahead for the two halves of the figure,
united at last in the Lake of the Universe.

title: The Place Where There Is No Darkness
content:
A brilliant satin shield protects the silent whispers of the night
An urban gradient taints the moon's enveloping cloak
The sky is blind to the stars, who hide behind an unwavering mask
Their light waiting behind a contrast-breaking curtain

The stars only dare to shine when there is nothing left to be seen
In a desert, on a plain, only miles and miles from the world
On no crowded street can one catch a glimpse of the heavens, shimmering overhead
For the city is as oblivious to the stars as a cartoon is to the viewer

title: The Remarkable Tendency of Things to Get Wet
content:
*I wrote this poem while sitting outside the Bell Pavilion in the misty morning rain, sipping coffee and counting the raindrops as they gathered in puddles. At the time, there was an ongoing Teamsters labor union strike at San Diego State University, and one could hear their chants as they marched across campus throughout the week.

As the clouds pour down their pitter-patter tears
to a grateful and mournful Earth,
early spring flowers spring up from their soggy roots
to remind you what they're worth.

Cheers arise from a chorus of poppies,
burning like foxfire on a misty green knoll,
while the highway hums with frustration and ire
as damp, seasoned pavement collects its grim toll.

Bare tables are sticky with fresh-fallen dew
and puddles collect at the sole of my shoe;
how deep--no, how shallow--these waters must be,
like a brackish lagoon where a river meets sea

The palm trees stand furrowed, disposed for a rest,
while underpaid workers do strike and protest
with their banners and chants boasting high in the air,
for an audience that won't even pretend to care.

All of this makes me wonder, before I forget,
is this really all? Do we get what we get?
So here do I sit, and here I reflect,
on the remarkable tendency of things to get wet.

title: Thoughts from the Aeroplane Bound for Dixie
content:
*This work represents my first attempt at what one might call "semi-automatic writing", wherein I essentially wrote down the first thing that came to mind. I wrote this while cruising at 35,000 feet over the desert southwest on a flight from San Diego to New Orleans (stop in Dallas). In summary, this work reflects my thoughts and feelings as I gazed out the window and daydreamed about my unfamiliar destination. In particular, my attention was captured by the clouds, farms, and canyon-crawled desert landscape sprawled out below me.

Hazy hues of summer seeds sown early in the season
scatter hastily above fractal mountains
and beneath my tender feet.

Panels of plight deck sand-kissed plains
where rigid hands perform treacherous work,
afraid, afraid of the storm that might never come.

A blanched, billowing border bisects and maims the divided land,
with an arbitrary air of impatient whimsy at its heel.

My nose itches as it inches and knows not where it is bound,
but for a false human name which it had been given
out of spite for the valley it had tarnished.

Aching canyons open their wounds
to show me the veins and sinew
that keep its blood flowing,
confiding in me their superficial secrets.

I clock a map and read the time from a magnet,
a circuit, a demon of the digital age,
thumping with ceaseless information,
but revealing very little.

The Earth opens her quarry-mouth wide
and offers her rich stone,
a haphazard gift
from a mother to her dying children.

A fall, to be sure, awaits me in Dallas,
but again I will sink to the lowly green skies,
their cottonwood hue trading moonlight for stardom.

And fall again I will,
to the wicked blue bayous of New Orleans,
where little awaits me but stories untold.

And as I stare at the silver strands
of cottonball whiskey,
between deisel-born tip-taps
and screen-age pitter patter,
I am reminded at once
of a moment that never came.

One at which life seemed like a marble on a hill,
vastly outworn by the twisted ides of tall grass
and gravity beneath its silky swirls
and solitary see-through sheen.

Like a die spinning wildly in the air,
I sat there, momentarily at rest,
and yet moving decisively against my will.

Life, it seems, is not fooled by "could have" or "would have",
these dirty lies we tell ourselves to escape the droll;
Instead, the dictates of fate conspire
to constantly deprive us of the illusion we call being.

Like an anxious electron,
you may know where you are,
or you may know where you are going,
but never both.

Cast down your bucket and see for yourself,
lest your reddish eyes be blinded
by the troubling tail lights of tomorrow.

title: Tire Pressure Sensor Fault
content:
I climb aboard my silver-steel wagon
and click the engine into roaring life.
The metallic choking subsides to a purr,
and the tiny digital display blinks alight.
On the dashboard, a warning flickers on,
bordered in hazard-orange:
"Tire Pressure Sensor Fault."
I press "OK" to dismiss, as I always do,
and proceed with no due caution,
because a broken sensor does no wrong
(unless the thing it's monitoring does).

And I place my phone above the cupholders
that seldom carry any weight,
tucked beneath the lip of the center console
whose hinge has recently been mended,
and beside the vacant silhouette
of what could once retain a cell phone,
but now could not fit widthwise
what it was meant to fit lengthwise.

And I grab the crooked handle
that sticks out from behind the steering wheel
and pull it towards me,
and then down a notch,
into reverse,
and then I release it;
and I gently maneuver
this two-ton beast
between crushed green plants
and a pristine Jeep;
and then I shift two more notches down,
reset the wheel,
and climb that asphalt ramp
that bridges my haven-like driveway
to the unpainted street.

And I cruise down High Valley,
its curves thrashing 'round
'tween the mounds and cliffs
that I've so often navigated,
and barely scrape by
the tameless bushes
that eerily creep
their fingers over the road,
occasionally brushing
against my hard skin.

And I hastily drive
to wherever I'm headed,
carelessly heeding
the rules of the road,
and I think for a moment
of the places I've been,
and the miles I've buried
beneath mountains of time,
and I remind myself at once
of the bright face that awaits me
just seven miles away.

title: Turtle
content:
A fat turtle loiters on a sun-baked stone
His shell a bleak brown-gray
Dry for a while, between lazy laps and nameless naps
His daily sojourn in a careless paradise.

As my eyes drift, a wild fence lizard catches my gaze,
Her soft-scaled torso gently oscillating with her breath,
As she scrambles and peers from a piecemeal ledge,
Keeping always on her feet, unable to sit still.

The leaves, as they sail to the Earth, leave ripples when they land in the pond,
Disturbing the elder koi as she patrols the shallow depths.
She sustains herself on water-bed greens and scraps from her royal subjects,
As she evades the snapping jaws and airborne claws that embattle her home.

And then I know,
As the turtle burrows into his hard rock home,
Beneath the half-broken shade of a winter-thinned tree,
And as the lizard traipses along the warm cobblestone wall,
Where only keenly-honed eyes can see,
And as the koi swims in hostile circuits,
Yearning for the blue-steel sea,
That I am one with the sedentary turtle, with the swift-legged lizard, and with the battle-scarred koi,
And that when I observe them,
With eyes glassy and naive,
I am looking at me.

title: Uncompromising Compromise
content:
If I can see it, why can't you?
If I should enjoy it, why shouldn't you, too?
Could it be that it's not? Could we ever be sure?
Is there nothing about it that begs your allure?

What makes you so sure? That I'm in the wrong?
From my side, it seems I've been right all along!
But what will you do? And why shall I care?
For you know there's little that I wouldn't dare.

So why do we fuss? Why do we fight?
We know we'll forget it all before tonight.
Just always remember, when you think I'm hight,
You'll always be wrong and I'll always be right.

title: Warm Vermont Night
content:
* I wrote this while sitting by the fireplace on a camping trip in southern Vermont.

The light from the fire danced on every surface it touched,
like the inverted image of an action hero
on the wall behind an onlooking audience.

The scent of burnt caramel invaded my nostrils,
seductive and crude in the lingering air,
like a newborn spring poppy or a ripe musk melon,
elusive and intimate, like faded childhood memories.

The hot coals gently roared and crackled
like a thousand distant lions, embattled,
or like a muscle-car engine burst, sizzling out,
as distance traded volume for tranquility.

The fire's warm hand caressed my cheek,
calling me into its tender embrace,
and as I reached blindly into that bright hive,
with embers buzzing like jealous bees,
the warm Vermont night pierced my hand
and buried its venom deep into my flesh.

title: Wicked Horizon
content:
The mountains and hills toss the sky above the horizon,
in a wicked roller coaster of terrain.
The sun uneasily climbs to the sky,
Afraid of what's to remain.

The sun knows it will set, the day knows it will end,
and it even knows how, it even knows when,
but the question the Sun can't stop asking again,
is what's on the other side?

For when one side is dark, the other is born,
The days and the nights, so beautifully torn,
Are threaded by needle, thread, and thorn,
In a fabric of perpetual change.

The day knows no start,
the day knows no end,
the day doesn't even try to pretend!
It just keeps on moving, like you, or like me,
And exactly that is all we must do.

title: Yesterdays Hence
content:
* Based on some thoughts I had while walking back to my apartment from the grocery store, knowing that I would soon move to the East Coast, not to return for several years.

The frigid air stung my eyes
as if to call me weak,
for tears that dance but dare not chance
to crawl across my cheek,

for the salty silver slivers
that never burned my eyes,
these wounds, disgraced, upon my face,
their pupils my disguise.

And then a question blinks alight
within my rampant mind,
of thoughts unsaid and books unread,
my duty in a bind,

and for a while I drift through dreams
of sultry summer Sundays,
but here, instead, I break my bread
on cold and callous Mondays.

For these dry days, someday too soon,
will be the "good 'ol days",
when autumn moons sang out their tunes
in amber-azure haze,

and then I'll see my present self
as "me, when I was younger";
nostalgic trips evoke my thirst,
for future years I hunger.

Beneath my feet, the desert churns,
above me, redwoods lumber;
a castle wall protects my hall,
where idle meanings slumber;

my left hand holds a crooked pen,
my right, a scroll of ash;
I've no recompense for yesterdays hence,
my rear regrets abashed.

title: You're In Love
content:
I hear childish voices taunt me:
"You're in love! You're in love!"
And at once, I can feel
the endearment they offer
as they validate my truth
that I am, indeed, in love.

And though I see through
the superstitions of my youth,
which whispered to me
in a sinister tone
that "the one" was nearby,
narrowly evading my gaze,

and in spite of my insistence
against fate and free will,
I still choose to believe,
in my heart of hearts,
that we are meant to be,
whatever that might mean.

Still I know,
despite the pale heartache
that darkens my day,
that at the end of my life
I'm promised a great peace
eternal, irrevocable, and absolute,

and yet I prefer
to persist and feel pain,
this strange, sick reminder
that I'm here and I can
feel the current's inescapable pull
and smell the breeze's sweet perfume.
